Crunchbase Startup Fundraising Analysis

A memory-conscious data engineering and analysis pipeline for historical Crunchbase startup investment data, using chunked processing, type optimisation and SQLite.

View GitHub ↗Open in Google Colab ↗
Executive overviewBusiness / analytical problemObjectiveApproachMethodologyKey insightsResults / conclusionsTechnical notes

Executive overview

The project processes and analyses a historical Crunchbase investment archive while keeping memory usage under tight constraints. The workflow combines incremental CSV processing, data cleaning, relational storage and SQL-based analysis.

Business / analytical problem

Large flat files can create unnecessary memory pressure when loaded in full. The analytical challenge was to preserve useful investment information while building a workflow that remained efficient enough for constrained environments.

Objective

Create a reproducible pipeline that cleans, optimises and stores startup investment data before extracting interpretable funding insights.

Approach

The data was read in 5,000-row chunks, structurally profiled, cleaned and downcast where appropriate. Uninformative high-overhead fields were removed before the data was migrated into SQLite.

Methodology

Python and Pandas handled incremental processing; SQLite provided the relational layer. Secondary indexes were created for selected analytical fields such as raised amount, company category and investor name.

Key insights

The analysis highlights a highly concentrated distribution of startup funding, stronger financing activity in technology-oriented sectors, and the institutional investors with the largest cumulative allocations in the dataset.

Results / conclusions

The final workflow separates data preparation from analysis and provides a compact relational base for repeatable SQL queries under constrained memory conditions.

Technical notes

The repository documents the chunk-processing strategy, type optimisation choices, encoding handling and SQLite schema/index design.
